source: Shem Tov Hebrew Matthew (Even Bochan, Ibn Shaprut c. 1385; critical text ed. G. Howard, base ms British Library Add. 26964)

verses.translation: At that{H1931} time{H6256} Yeshua{H3442} passed{H5674} through the standing grain{H7054} on the day{H3117} of the Shabbat{H7676}, and his disciples{H8527}, being hungry{H7457}, began{H2490} to pluck{H6131} the ears{H7641} and to rub them between{H996} their hands{H3027} and to eat{H398} them.

one_way_hebrew: בקמות — 'in the standing grain': קמה (H7054) is the exact word of the statute that governs this scene, Deut 23:26 — 'when thou comest into the standing corn (בקמת) of thy neighbour, thou mayest pluck the ears with thine hand.' The Hebrew reader sees at once that the disciples are doing what the Torah expressly permits; the whole dispute is about Shabbat, not about taking. Greek σπορίμων ('sown fields') loses the statute-word.
שבולים (H7641) — the ears of Gen 41's dream and Ruth 2's gleaning; לעקור ('pluck up') and לפרוך ('rub, crush') are living agricultural Hebrew.
greek_deviations: 'And to RUB them between their hands' — Greek Matthew lacks the rubbing; it is Luke 6:1's detail (ψώχοντες ταῖς χερσίν, 'rubbing them in their hands'). The Hebrew Matthew again agrees with Luke against Greek Matthew (cf. 24:37).
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק נ״ב (Perek 52) begins here (recorded in the ms after 11:30).
The scan reads ביום השבת ('on the day of the Shabbat'); the circulating transcription's מיום is a typo, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (12:1): ותלמידיו] תלמידיו B; התחילו] התחיל C.

verses.translation: And the Pharisees{H6567} saw{H7200} it and said{H559} to him: Behold{H2009}, your disciples{H8527} are doing{H6213} a thing{H1697} that is not proper{H3559} to do on the day{H3117} of the Shabbat{H7676}.

one_way_hebrew: פרושים — 'the separated ones' (פרש, H6567): the party's own Hebrew name, of which Greek Φαρισαῖοι is a transliteration.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (12:2): נכון] הגון F, omit G; הפרושים] הפרושין F; ויראו] + אותם F.

verses.translation: And Yeshua{H3442} answered{H6030} them: Have you not read{H7121} what David{H1732} did{H6213} when he was hungry{H7457}, and his men{H582},

textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (12:3): ולא] לא B; שעשה] עשה ABDG; רעב] + הוא A.

verses.translation: in the house{H1004} of Elohim{H430}, when they ate{H398} of the bread{H3899} of the Presence{H6440} — in the foreign tongue{H3937}, pan sagrah — which is not eaten{H398} except by the priests{H3548} alone{H905}?

one_way_hebrew: לחם הפנים — 'the bread of the Presence,' the Torah's own term (Exod 25:30; 1 Sam 21:7, David's very episode). The text then glosses it בלעז פא״ן סאג״רה — Romance 'pan sagrah' ('holy bread') — for readers who knew the church's vocabulary, exactly like the evangeli gloss at 24:14: the Hebrew term is native, the foreign word is the visitor. Greek ἄρτους τῆς προθέσεως is itself a translation of the Hebrew phrase.
textual_notes: ms writes אלקים with the reverent ק-spelling.
Howard's apparatus (12:4): בלעז] לעז ABDEF; the gloss varies — שאגרט A, שאגראט B, שאגראטו D, שגראש EF, omitted with פאן in G; האלקים] האלים A.

verses.translation: And also in the Torah{H8451} have you not read{H7121} that the priests{H3548} in the house{H1004} of the Sanctuary{H4720} sometimes{H6471} profane{H2490} the Shabbatot{H7676} and have no sin{H2399}?

one_way_hebrew: מחללים (H2490, chalal) — 'profane': the Torah's own verb for Shabbat-violation (מחלליה מות יומת, Exod 31:14). The argument is a priestly halakhic one — Temple service overrides Shabbat (Num 28:9-10, the doubled Shabbat offering) — stated in the Torah's own terms.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (12:5): השבתות] השבת EF.

verses.translation: Amen{H543}, I say{H559} to you that the Sanctuary{H4720} is greater{H1419} than it{H4480}.

translation_notes: Two construals of שמקדש גדול ממנו הוא: 'the Sanctuary is greater than it' — than the Shabbat-plucking matter at issue (so Howard: 'the temple is greater than this') — or, taking הוא as the subject, 'greater than the Sanctuary is HE.' Greek Matthew reads 'something greater than the Sanctuary is here' (μεῖζον τοῦ ἱεροῦ). Either way, the Hebrew argues from the Sanctuary's overriding weight in the law, continuing v. 5.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (12:6): הוא] + זה A, omit G.

verses.translation: If{H432} you had known{H3045} what this is — kindness{H2617} I desire{H2654}, and not sacrifice{H2077} — you would not have condemned{H2325} the blameless{H8549}.

one_way_hebrew: חסד חפצתי ולא זבח — Hos 6:6 quoted in Hosea's own consonants. Greek ἔλεος θέλω καὶ οὐ θυσίαν translates the verse; the Hebrew text carries it. And התמימים — 'the BLAMELESS' (תמים, H8549), the Torah's word for the unblemished offering and the whole-hearted walker (Gen 6:9; Ps 19:14) — where Greek has τοὺς ἀναιτίους ('the guiltless'): the disciples are declared not merely innocent but tamim.
translation_notes: זבה — the base ms writes זבה for זבח (ה/ח interchange, another inner-Hebrew copying slip); mss ABDEFG read זבח, and Howard prints '(sacrifice).'
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (12:7): זבה] זבח ABDEFG; מהו] מהוא B, כי G.

verses.translation: For the Son{H1121} of Man{H120} is lord{H113} of the Shabbat{H7676}.

greek_deviations: The Hebrew states it without the Greek's 'for the Son of man is lord EVEN of the sabbath' (καὶ γάρ... καί) — no concession that the Shabbat is a lesser thing to be lorded over; the sentence simply seats the Son of Man as the Shabbat's master, closing the halakhic argument of vv. 3-7.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (12:8): אדם] האדם EF; השבת] השמים EF — mss EF read 'lord of HEAVEN.'

verses.translation: And it came to pass{H1961} at the end{H7117} of the days{H3117}, Yeshua{H3442} passed on{H5674} from there{H8033} and entered{H935} into their houses{H1004} of assembly.

one_way_hebrew: בתי כנסיות — 'houses of assembly,' the native Hebrew name for synagogues (beit knesset); Greek συναγωγή is the Greek dress of the same institution.
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק נ״ג (Perek 53) begins here.
Howard's apparatus (12:9): כנסיותם] כנסיותהם A, כנסיותיהם D.

verses.translation: And there{H8033} was a man{H120} with his hand{H3027} withered{H3002}, and they asked him{H7592}, saying{H559}: Is it permitted on the Shabbat{H7676} to heal him{H7495}?

one_way_hebrew: מותר — 'permitted': the halakhic term of rabbinic Hebrew (mutar/asur), the native idiom of a Shabbat question; Greek εἰ ἔξεστιν translates the category.
ידו יבשה — the withered hand of 1 Kgs 13:4, Jeroboam's hand that 'dried up' (ותיבש ידו) at the altar — the same words.
greek_deviations: Greek Matthew adds the motive 'that they might accuse him' (ἵνα κατηγορήσωσιν αὐτοῦ); the Shem Tov text has no such clause — the question stands as a question. The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew carries the motive ('in order that they could slander him'), with the Greek.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (12:10): וישאלוהו] וישאלוה A, וישאלהו EF.

verses.translation: And he said{H559} to them: Who{H4310} among you has{H3426} one{H259} sheep{H6629} — and it falls{H5307} into a pit{H7745} on the day{H3117} of the Shabbat{H7676} — and will not raise it up{H6965}?

one_way_hebrew: שוחה (H7745) — the dug pit of Jer 18:20,22 ('they have digged a pit for my soul') and Prov 26:27; Greek βόθυνον translates. יקימנה — 'raise it up' (קום), the verb of Deut 22:4, the Torah's own command to lift a fallen animal: the argument stands on a statute the hearers must obey.

verses.translation: How much more a man{H120}, who is better{H2896} than it! Therefore it is permitted to do{H6213} — and one ought{H3426}, for a man, to do what is more{H3148} good{H2896} on the Shabbat{H7676}.

one_way_hebrew: כ״ש — the ms abbreviates כל שכן, 'how much more': the rabbinic qal va-chomer formula, written with scribal gershayim exactly as in any halakhic text. The whole verse argues in the forms of the beit midrash — מותר ('permitted'), לפיכך ('therefore'), יש לאדם ('one is obligated'); Greek ὥστε ἔξεστιν flattens the legal register.
greek_deviations: The Hebrew goes beyond the Greek's 'it is lawful to do well on the sabbath': ויש לאדם לעשות יותר טוב — it is permitted AND ONE OUGHT to do the better thing on Shabbat. Howard renders 'it is permissible and [necessary] for man to do better on the Sabbath.' Healing on Shabbat is not a concession but a duty — the symbol deepens the command, it does not dissolve it.

verses.translation: Then{H227} he said{H559} to the man{H376}: Stretch out{H5186} your hand{H3027}. And he stretched out{H5186} his hand, and it returned{H7725} like{H3644} the other{H312}.

one_way_hebrew: ותשב — 'and it RETURNED' (שוב): the healing verb of 1 Kgs 13:6, where Jeroboam's dried-up hand 'returned to him (ותשב) and became as it was before' — the same scene-pair as v. 10's ידו יבשה: the Hebrew tells the synagogue healing in the words of the altar healing.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (12:13): ותשב] וישב EF.

verses.translation: And then{H227} the Pharisees{H6567} took counsel together{H3245} and plotted{H5230} against him, to put him to death{H4191}.

one_way_hebrew: נוסדו (H3245) — Ps 2:2's own verb: 'the rulers take counsel together (נוסדו יחד) against YHWH and against his Mashiach.' וינכלו (H5230, nakal) — Gen 37:18: Joseph's brothers 'conspired against him to slay him' (ויתנכלו אתו להמיתו) — the same verb AND the same infinitive להמיתו. In two words the Hebrew sets the plot inside Psalm 2 and the Joseph story; Greek συμβούλιον ἔλαβον ('took counsel') carries neither.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (12:14): וינכלו] ויתנכלו EF (the exact Gen 37:18 form); אליו] omit D.

verses.translation: And it came to pass{H1961} after{H310} this{H2063}, Yeshua{H3442} knew{H3045} it and turned aside{H5186} from there{H8033}, and many{H7227} sick{H2470} went{H1980} after him{H310}, and he healed{H7495} all of them{H3605}.

textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק נ״ד (Perek 54) begins here.
Howard's apparatus (12:15): זאת] כן EF; וידע ישו] transposed H; ויט] ועבר H; וירפא] והוא רפא H.

verses.translation: And he commanded them{H6680}, saying{H559}, not to{H1077} reveal him{H1540}.

textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (12:16): mss vary between יגלהו and יפרסמוהו ('publicize him') for יגלוהו; לאמר omitted in H.

verses.translation: to establish{H6965} what was spoken{H559} by the hand of Yeshayah{H3470}:

translation_notes: ע״י — the ms abbreviates על ידי ('by the hand of'), the Hebrew citation idiom (cf. ביד עבדיו הנביאים, 2 Kgs 24:2); ישעה — Yeshayah spelled defectively (mss AB ישעיה).
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (12:17): לקיים] בעבור שיתקיים CDEFGH; ישעה] ישעיה AB, ישעוה H.

verses.translation: Behold{H2005} my lad{H5288} whom I have chosen{H977}, my chosen one{H972} in whom my soul{H5315} is pleased{H7521}; I will put{H5414} my spirit{H7307} upon him, and he will declare{H5046} judgment{H4941} to the nations{H1471}.

one_way_hebrew: The citation is Isa 42:1 in Hebrew — בחירי רצתה נפשי... רוחי עליו... משפט לגוים are Isaiah's own words. Where MT reads עבדי ('my servant'), the base text reads נערי ('my LAD' — the beloved boy of the household, Gen 22:5); mss DEFH read עבדי with MT. Greek Matthew's ὁ παῖς μου ('my boy/servant') sits exactly between the two — παῖς is how a Hebrew נער sounds in Greek.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (12:18): נערי] עבדי DEFH; ומשפט] משפט EF.

verses.translation: And he will not fear{H7297}, and he will not run{H7323}, and no one{H259} will hear{H8085} him in the street{H2351}.

one_way_hebrew: ולא ירוץ — 'he will not RUN': MT Isa 42:4 reads לא יכהה ולא ירוץ ('he shall not grow dim nor be crushed/run'); the Shem Tov line conflates Isa 42:2 and 42:4 as a Hebrew reader's memory does, keeping Isaiah's own rare verb. ירהה (H7297, rahah) — 'fear', the verb of Isa 44:8 (תרהו), two chapters on in the same servant-cycle. Greek Matthew ('he shall not strive nor cry') translates 42:2 only.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (12:19): בחוץ] + קולו ABCDEF ('his voice,' completing Isa 42:2); ירהה] ירהא A, יכבה G. Howard: 'He will not fear nor will he run nor shall one hear (his voice) in the street.'

verses.translation: A crushed{H7533} reed{H7070} he will not break{H7665}, and a dim{H3544} wick{H6594} he will not quench{H3518}, until{H5704} he sets{H7760} judgment{H4941} forever{H5331}.

one_way_hebrew: קנה רצוץ לא ישבור ופשתה כהה לא יכבנה — Isa 42:3 verbatim, letter for letter. And the close keeps Isaiah's verb: עד ישים... משפט — Isa 42:4's עד ישים בארץ משפט ('till he have SET judgment in the earth'). Greek Matthew reads 'till he send forth (ἐκβάλῃ) judgment unto victory,' and mss ABDEFG assimilate to it with ישליך ('cast forth') — the base text stands with Isaiah against the Greek.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (12:20): ישים] ישליך ABDEFG; ישים לנצח] transposed C.

verses.translation: And in his name{H8034} the nations{H1471} will hope{H3176}.

one_way_hebrew: ייחלו (H3176, yachal) — Isaiah's own hoping verb (MT Isa 42:4 ייחילו). The clause reads 'in his NAME shall the NATIONS hope' where MT reads 'the isles shall wait for his TORAH' — the same substitution found in LXX Isaiah and Greek Matthew; the Shem Tov text carries that citation-form in Hebrew, keeping Isaiah's verb.

verses.translation: Then{H227} there was brought{H935} before him{H6440} a man{H120}, blind{H5787} and mute{H483}, with the demon{H7700} within him{H8432}, and he healed{H7495} him — and they saw{H7200},

textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק נ״ה (Perek 55) begins here.
The scan reads אדם; the circulating transcription's אדמ (final-mem misprint) is corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (12:22): וראו] וראה ABDEFGH; לפניו] לפני ישו G; אחד] omit H.

verses.translation: and the crowds{H2267} were amazed{H6381} and said{H559}: Is this{H2088} not the Son{H1121} of David{H1732}?

one_way_hebrew: ונפלאו (H6381, pala) — 'were made to wonder': the root of פלא, the wonder-word of Exod 15:11 and Ps 118:23 ('this is YHWH's doing; it is marvellous — נפלאת — in our eyes').

verses.translation: And the Pharisees{H6567}, quick{H7925} to hear{H8085} it, said{H559}: This one{H2088} does not cast out{H3318} the demons{H7700} except by Baal{H1168} Zevuv{H2070}, master{H1167} of the demons.

one_way_hebrew: בעל זבוב — 2 Kgs 1:2-6's god of Ekron by his Hebrew name ('lord of flies'), and the base text calls him בעל השדים, 'MASTER of the demons' — a deliberate Hebrew play: baal of flies, baal of demons. Greek transliterates Βεελζεβούλ and reads ἄρχοντι ('prince'); mss ABDEFG assimilate with שר ('prince'). The pun exists only in Hebrew.
וישכימו (H7925, shakam) — literally 'rose early': the Hebrew idiom for eager haste (Jer 7:13, 'rising up early and speaking'); Howard renders 'were quick to hear.'
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (12:24): the other mss read simply וישמעו ('and the Pharisees heard'); בעל 2°] שר ABDEFG; השדים 1°] שדים BG.

verses.translation: And Yeshua{H3442} knew{H3045} their thoughts{H4284} and said{H559} to them in a parable{H4912}: Every kingdom{H4438} divided among you will be made desolate{H8074}, and so every city{H5892} and house{H1004} on which division falls{H5307} within them{H8432} will not stand{H6965}.

one_way_hebrew: במשל — the Hebrew names the form: a MASHAL (H4912), Ezekiel's genre word (Ezek 17:2); Greek Matthew 12:25 has no parable-notice at all. And מחלוקת — 'division' — is the rabbinic term (machaloket) for a divided house or school: native legal-academic Hebrew.
תשומם (H8074, shamem) — 'will be made desolate': the desolation root of Dan 9:27 and Lev 26:31; Greek ἐρημοῦται translates it.
textual_notes: The scan reads מחלוקת (first occurrence); the circulating transcription's מחלוקה is a typo, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (12:25): מחשבותם ישו] transposed ABDEFGH; שביניכם] שביניהם A and most mss ('among them'); ובית] או בית A; בתוכם] בנהם A; מחלוקת 2°] מחלוקתם F, מחלוקות E.

verses.translation: And if the satan{H7854} casts out{H3318} another{H312} satan — division among you! — how{H349} will his kingdom{H4438} stand{H5975}?

one_way_hebrew: שטן (H7854) — the accuser by his Hebrew name (Job 1:6; Zech 3:1-2); the Hebrew can say 'the satan casts out another satan' because שטן is a common noun — adversary — before it is a name. Greek ὁ Σατανᾶς τὸν Σατανᾶν must treat it as a frozen loanword.
translation_notes: ביניכם — the base ms reads 'division among YOU' (as at v. 25), turning the analysis into a barb at the accusers; most mss read ביניהם ('among them'), and Howard renders '(them).' ואת — the base's opening particle is odd; ms A reads ואם ('and if'), which the sense requires and the translation follows.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (12:26): ואת] ואם A; שטן 2°] השטן C; ביניכם] בנהם A, ביניהם BDEFGH.

verses.translation: And if{H518} I cast out{H3318} the demons{H7700} by Baal{H1168} Zevuv{H2070} — your own sons{H1121}, why do they not cast them out{H3318}? And for this{H2088} they will be your judges{H8199}.

textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (12:27): בנים] omit GH; לא] omit F; הוציאם] הוציאום ADEFH, תוציאום G.

verses.translation: But if{H518} I cast out{H3318} the demons{H7700} by the spirit{H7307} of Elohim{H430}, truly{H571} the end{H7093} of the kingdom{H4438} has come{H935}.

greek_deviations: A reading found nowhere in the Greek tradition: Greek Matthew has 'then the kingdom of God is come upon you' (ἔφθασεν ἐφ' ὑμᾶς ἡ βασιλεία τοῦ θεοῦ); the Hebrew reads באמת בא קץ מלכות — 'truly the END (קץ) of the kingdom has come.' Read with v. 26 ('how will HIS kingdom stand?'), the sentence announces the end of the satan's kingdom: the exorcisms are its death-notice. Howard renders 'truly the end of [his] kingdom has come.' קץ is Daniel's appointed-end word (Dan 8:19; 11:27; 12:13); the sentence carries Daniel's eschatology, not the Greek's. The Vat. Ebr. 100 Hebrew Matthew reads 'did not the heavenly kingdom come among you,' with the Greek.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (12:28): the mss diverge widely as scribes pull the clause toward the Greek — G reads באמת מלכות שמים, EF add אלקים after קץ, A adds ומלכותו, D omits באמת...מלכות; the base text stands alone with בא קץ מלכות.

verses.translation: And how{H349} can{H3201} a man{H376} enter{H935} the house{H1004} of a mighty one{H1368} to take{H3947} his vessels{H3627}, unless he binds{H7194} him first{H8462}? And afterward he will plunder{H7997} his house.

one_way_hebrew: גבור (H1368) — the Tanakh's 'mighty man'; the scene tracks Isa 49:24-25, 'shall the prey be taken from the mighty (מגבור)?... even the captives of the mighty shall be taken away' — the very oracle behind the saying, visible only through the shared word. ישלול (H7997) — the plunder verb of Isa 10:6.
textual_notes: The scan reads גבור ('mighty one'); the circulating transcription's גבול ('border') is a typo, corrected here.
Howard's apparatus (12:29): בביתו] ביתו ABDGH; ואח״כ] ואחר ABDEFGH.

verses.translation: Whoever{H4310} is not with me{H5978} is against me{H5048}; he who does not join himself{H2266} with me{H5973} denies me in deed{H6467}.

greek_deviations: Greek: 'he that gathereth not with me scattereth' (σκορπίζει). The Hebrew: מי שלא יתחבר עמי יכפור בפועל — 'whoever does not JOIN himself to me DENIES in deed': not failed harvesting but practical denial — the refusal of fellowship is itself a confession. Vat. Ebr. 100 reads 'scatters against me,' with the Greek.
translation_notes: יכפור — the rabbinic sense of כפר, 'to deny' (as in כופר בעיקר, one who denies the root); בפועל — 'in deed, in practice' (פועל, H6467). Mss ABEF read בי ('denies ME'); Howard: 'denies (me).'
textual_notes: Shem Tov's own section heading פרק נ״ו (Perek 56) begins here.
Howard's apparatus (12:30): בפועל] בי ABEF, במעל DG ('in treachery'); יתחבר] מתחבר EF; שלא] שאינו BDG; מה] ומי AEF.

verses.translation: Therefore{H3651} I say{H559} to you that every{H3605} sin{H2399} and blasphemy{H1421} will be forgiven to the sons{H1121} of man{H120}, but blasphemy{H1421} of the Spirit{H7307} will not be forgiven.

one_way_hebrew: ימחל — מחל, the rabbinic forgiveness verb (mechilah), the living Hebrew of the prayerbook ('forgive us — מחל לנו'); Greek ἀφεθήσεται. גדוף (H1421) — the reviling word of Isa 51:7 and Zeph 2:8.
textual_notes: Howard's apparatus (12:31): כן] על כן ABEF; ימחל] ימחול B (and DG at the second occurrence).

verses.translation: And everyone who says{H559} a word{H1697} against{H5048} the Son{H1121} of Man{H120}, it will be forgiven him; but everyone who says a word against the Holy{H6918} Spirit{H7307}, it will not be forgiven him — not in this world and not in the world to come.

one_way_hebrew: בעה״ז ולא בעה״ב — העולם הזה and העולם הבא, abbreviated with scribal gershayim exactly as in any responsum: THE rabbinic doctrine-pair 'this world / the world to come.' Greek spells it out (οὔτε ἐν τούτῳ τῷ αἰῶνι οὔτε ἐν τῷ μέλλοντι); a Hebrew author writes עה״ז/עה״ב by reflex — a translator from Greek does not invent scribal abbreviations.

verses.translation: Make{H6213} a tree{H6086} good{H2896} according to good fruit{H6529}, or a tree bad{H7451} according to bad fruit — for the truth{H571} is: from{H4480} the fruit{H6529} the tree{H6086} is known{H3045}.

verses.translation: I say{H559} to you that for all{H3605} the words{H1697} which a man{H120} speaks{H1696}, he is bound{H2325} to give{H5414} an accounting{H2808} in the day{H3117} of judgment{H1779}.

verses.translation: According to{H5921} your words{H1697} you will be judged{H8199}, and according to your deeds{H4639} you will be convicted{H2325}.

greek_deviations: Greek Matthew rests both clauses on words: 'by thy words thou shalt be justified, and by thy words thou shalt be condemned.' The Hebrew splits them: by your WORDS you are judged — brought to trial — and by your DEEDS (מעשיך) you are convicted. Judgment weighs what a man DID; speech opens the case, works close it. Vat. Ebr. 100 ('saved because of your words or destroyed because of your words') sides with the Greek — the Shem Tov base stands alone with the deeds-clause, and it is the Torah's own standard (Jer 17:10, 'to give every man according to his ways, and according to the fruit of his doings').
textual_notes: על פי — 'according to the mouth of': the Torah's evidentiary idiom (על פי שנים עדים, Deut 17:6) — a court phrase for a court verse.

verses.translation: For as{H834} he was{H1961} in the bowels{H4578} of the fish{H1710} three days{H3117} and three nights{H3915}, so{H3651} will the Son{H1121} of Man{H120} be in the belly{H990} of the earth{H776} three days{H3117} and three nights{H3915}, in the grave{H6913}.

one_way_hebrew: במעי הדגה — Jonah's own words: Jonah 2:1, במעי הדגה (with the feminine דגה, exactly as here); and בבטן answers Jonah 2:3, מבטן שאול ('out of the BELLY of Sheol I cried'). The Hebrew keeps Jonah's chain — belly of the fish, belly of Sheol, belly of the earth — where Greek καρδίᾳ τῆς γῆς ('heart of the earth') breaks it.
ג׳ ימים וג׳ לילות — the ms writes the numerals with scribal geresh (ג׳), as Hebrew scribes do; three days AND three nights, Jonah 2:1's full count, stands in the text as the sign's explicit measure.
greek_deviations: The Hebrew closes with בקבר — 'in the GRAVE': the sign of Yonah is pinned to the tomb itself, three days and three nights of burial. No Greek witness carries the word.

chapter_notes.summary: Matthew 12 in the Shem Tov Hebrew is the Shabbat-and-kingdom chapter, and its distinctive readings run one direction. (1) 12:28 reads 'truly the END (קץ) of the kingdom has come' — read with v. 26 ('how will HIS kingdom stand?'), the exorcisms announce the end of the satan's kingdom, where Greek Matthew has 'the kingdom of God is come upon you'; the mss scatter trying to restore the Greek. (2) 12:37 reads 'by your words you will be judged and by your DEEDS (מעשיך) you will be convicted' — Greek rests both clauses on words alone. (3) 12:1's בקמות is Deut 23:26's own statute-word for plucking ears in standing grain, and 'rubbing them between their hands' agrees with Luke 6:1 against Greek Matthew; 12:12 makes Shabbat-good a positive duty ('it is permitted AND ONE OUGHT to do the better thing'). (4) 12:7 quotes Hos 6:6 in Hosea's consonants and calls the disciples תמימים ('blameless'). (5) 12:14 tells the plot in Ps 2:2's verb (נוסדו) and Gen 37:18's verb-plus-infinitive (וינכלו... להמיתו — Joseph's brothers). (6) The Isa 42 citation (12:18-21) keeps Isaiah's עד ישים ('till he SET judgment,' Isa 42:4) where mss ABDEFG assimilate to the Greek's 'cast forth' (ישליך); base reads נערי ('my lad') for MT's 'my servant.' (7) 12:40 keeps Jonah's own vocabulary (במעי הדגה, בטן) and adds בקבר — 'three days and three nights IN THE GRAVE.' (8) The vernacular glosses multiply — pan sagrah for the showbread (12:4), Rezinah de Isteriah for the queen of Sheba (12:42), and mss EF gloss even 'dry places' (12:43) — annotations intelligible only if the Hebrew is the host text. (9) The chapter's frame is rabbinic Hebrew throughout: כ״ש (qal va-chomer, 12:12), מותר, עה״ז/עה״ב (12:32), מחל, יום הדין and din ve-cheshbon (12:36), machaloket (12:25). (10) 12:24's Baal-zevuv / baal-hashedim pun and 12:34's פתנים (Ps 58's deaf adder) live only in Hebrew. Shem Tov's section divisions fall at vv. 1 (Perek 52), 9 (53), 15 (54), 22 (55), 30 (56), 38 (57), and 46 (58).
